body:
### Problem

`vim.wait(timeout, pred)` does not return at `timeout` when every call of `pred` leaves a pending close callback, for example by closing a `vim.uv` timer. Each loop pass then returns without blocking and takes under 1 ms, and the elapsed-time accounting drops it, so the wait never ends: we measured about 3 million predicate calls over 115 s with a 15 s timeout.

A common real-world shape is a predicate that makes an RPC through a helper that arms a timeout timer per request (`new_timer`, `start`, `stop`, `close`).

### Steps to reproduce

`nvim --clean --headless -l repro.lua`:

```lua
local uv = vim.uv
local function run(label, pred)
  local t0 = uv.hrtime()
  local ok = vim.wait(500, pred)
  print(("%s returned=%s elapsed_ms=%d"):format(label, tostring(ok), (uv.hrtime() - t0) / 1e6))
end
local function busy(ns) local s = uv.hrtime() + ns; while uv.hrtime() < s do end end

run("plain", function() return false end)
run("close+1.5ms", function() uv.new_timer():close(); busy(1.5e6); return false end)
-- never returns:
run("close", function() local t = uv.new_timer(); t:start(60000, 0, function() end); t:stop(); t:close(); return false end)
print("unreachable on 0.11.7 and 0.12.5")
```

### Expected behavior

All three waits return `false` after about 500 ms, and the final line prints.

### Actual behavior (macOS arm64; identical on 0.11.7 and 0.12.5)

```
plain returned=false elapsed_ms=503
close+1.5ms returned=false elapsed_ms=761
<hangs; killed after 8 s>
```

`close+1.5ms` shows the accounting: 500 passes of about 1.5 ms each were counted as 1 ms each, so the 500 ms wait took 761 ms. With a pass under 1 ms, each counts 0. A `vim.schedule(function() end)` per predicate call hangs the same way. Keeping one timer and only starting and stopping it does not hang.

### Cause

`LOOP_PROCESS_EVENTS_UNTIL` (used by `nlua_wait`) subtracts the whole elapsed milliseconds of each pass and then resets its baseline, discarding the sub-millisecond remainder every pass:
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/659164699f8d884a90b23829c0a0c5cc1ab38873/src/nvim/event/multiqueue.h#L35-L37

```c
uint64_t now = os_hrtime();
remaining -= (int64_t)((now - before) / 1000000);
before = now;
```

### Suggested fix

Take a fixed deadline once (`deadline = os_hrtime() + timeout * 1000000`) and compute `remaining = (deadline - os_hrtime()) / 1000000` on each pass. A minimal alternative is to count at least 1 ms per pass (round each pass up), which guarantees termination but ends waits slightly early when passes are fast.

### Nvim version

NVIM v0.11.7 and v0.12.5 (macOS arm64)
title: vim.wait() never times out when each predicate call closes a libuv handle
